summary: Stocks pulled back and gave back part of Monday's bounce; gold led the move lower. The Nasdaq fell about 2 percent and lost its hourly trend stop, while the S&P held up far better and closed back above its 50-hour average. Gold was the biggest mover, down about 2.3 percent and below its trend stop; crude went the other way, up about 1.6 percent and reclaiming its stop. Volatility eased to about 26 after a brief tag of 29. Theme of the day: Gold on its own.

risk.note: Both equity hourly trend stops flipped overhead and gold lost its stop, so the short-term trend turned down even though the session balanced. Wait for acceptance (two one-hour closes) before leaning on a break. Week ahead: holiday-shortened week; pre-holiday data Wednesday (durable goods, the GDP revision, PCE inflation, jobless claims), closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, early close Friday; next policy event the December FOMC.

psychology: After a big up day like Monday, the instinct is to assume the bounce just keeps going. Today punished that. Price broke the opening-range high in the first fifteen minutes, then failed and spent the day drifting back inside the range. The lesson: a break is not a trend until price holds it. Wait for acceptance, meaning two full one-hour candles beyond the level, before you trust a move. Chasing the first poke is how good setups turn into bad trades.
